source_title: South Korea’s AI Bubble Just Popped

claims.quote: South Korea had the best-performing stock market in the world
claims.claim: [As of about three weeks before this video's publication, i.e. late June/early July 2026] South Korea's KOSPI was the best-performing major stock market in the world.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: CNBC described the KOSPI as 'the world's best-performing stock market this year' as of July 9, 2026, matching the period referenced. https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/09/kospi-bear-territory-ai-samsung-skhynix-chipmakers.html

claims.quote: it's gone up almost 200% in the last 12 months
claims.claim: [The KOSPI] rose almost 200% in the 12 months leading up to its June 2026 peak.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: KOSPI rose from 3,188.07 (18 Jul 2025) to a record close of 9,114.55 (22 Jun 2026) = +185.9%, measured to the pre-crash peak the video refers to as '3 weeks ago'. Bloomberg independently used the same framing: 'the Kospi surging close to 200% over the last 12 months'. https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-06-25/south-korea-s-ant-army-is-driving-an-ai-market-frenzy

claims.quote: which only made 24%
claims.claim: Over the same trailing-12-month window [ending at the KOSPI's June 2026 peak], the US S&P 500 returned only 24%.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: S&P 500 5,967.84 (18 Jul 2025) to 7,472.79 (22 Jun 2026) = +25.2%, close to the stated 24% on the same basis as the KOSPI comparison. Yahoo Finance index price history.

claims.quote: Samsung, was up over 500%
claims.claim: [At its 52-week trough-to-peak point in 2026] Samsung Electronics stock was up over 500%.
claims.label: misleading
claims.basis: 52-week trough-to-peak: roughly 67,500 -> 374,500 KRW ≈ +455%, short of the claimed 'over 500%' even on the most charitable (trough-to-peak) basis. A trailing-12-month-to-peak framing (~+506%) would clear it, but that is not 'at one point this year'. investing.com Samsung Electronics historical price data.

claims.quote: SK Hynix was up over 1,000%
claims.claim: [At its 52-week trough-to-peak point in 2026] SK Hynix stock was up over 1,000% ('basically a 10x').
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: 52-week trough-to-peak: roughly 245,000 -> 2,987,000 KRW ≈ +1,119%, comfortably clearing 'over 1,000%'/10x. 'At one point X was up over N%' is a trough-to-peak measure over the 52-week window, not a trailing point-to-point return — using the wrong basis is what causes this specific claim to get misjudged false. investing.com SK Hynix historical price data.

claims.quote: the top 10 companies represent 36% of this index
claims.claim: [In the S&P 500 / VOO ETF] the top 10 companies represent 36% of the index, a historically high concentration.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Top-10 S&P 500 share was about 36.4% as of late May 2026, vs about 23% at the 2000 dot-com peak. https://en.macromicro.me/series/46222/share-of-sp500-top10-companies-total-market-cap

claims.quote: represent over 56% of their whole stock market
claims.claim: [Samsung and SK Hynix] represent over 56% of the whole KOSPI (South Korea's stock market).
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Combined Samsung+SK Hynix weight in the KOSPI crossed 50% in late May 2026 and reached roughly 60% by late June/July 2026; 56% sits inside that trajectory for mid-July 2026, when this video was recorded. https://en.sedaily.com/finance/2026/05/27/samsung-sk-hynix-surge-alone-as-chip-duo-tops-half-of-kospi

claims.quote: roughly 14 million retail investors
claims.claim: About 14 million people in South Korea are retail investors.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Bloomberg reports approximately 14 million retail investors in South Korea as of mid-2026. https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-06-25/south-korea-s-ant-army-is-driving-an-ai-market-frenzy

claims.quote: in just 21 days, everything started to collapse. The KOSPI dropped 25%
claims.claim: After its June 2026 peak, the KOSPI dropped 25% over a span of 21 days.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: KOSPI record close 9,114.55 (22 Jun 2026) to 6,806.93 (13 Jul 2026) = -25.3%, and 22 Jun to 13 Jul is 21 days — matches almost exactly. Yahoo Finance ^KS11 daily closes.

claims.quote: 1.2 million accounts
claims.claim: 1.2 million South Korean brokerage accounts got hit with margin call thresholds during the KOSPI crash.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Multiple outlets report more than 1.2 million retail leveraged-credit accounts triggered margin calls as of mid-July 2026. https://easternherald.com/2026/07/20/south-korea-margin-loans-retail-investors-kospi-crash/

claims.quote: one in every 30 people in the country
claims.claim: 1.2 million margin-called accounts in South Korea works out to one in every 30 people in the country.
claims.label: false
claims.basis: 1.2M / ~51.7M South Korean population is 1-in-43, not 1-in-30 (1-in-30 would need ~1.7M accounts). The ratio is only close to 1-in-30 (33.4) against the ~35.9M working-age (15-64) population, but the claim says 'people in the country', which reads as total population — so the arithmetic as stated doesn't reconcile with either population figure it could plausibly mean. Population: https://www.worldometers.info/world-population/south-korea-population/

claims.quote: over 3 trillion won in investments were liquidated
claims.claim: Over 3 trillion won in investments were liquidated during the KOSPI crash.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: July 2026 forced liquidations reached 3.442 trillion KRW. https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/south-korean-stock-market-faces-margin-call-crisis-july-forced-liquidation-reaches-3-442-trillion-krw

claims.quote: 320,000 accounts were just wiped out, some of them overnight
claims.claim: 320,000 South Korean brokerage accounts were wiped out during the crash, some overnight.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Multiple outlets report 320,000-360,000 accounts forcibly liquidated. https://finance.biggo.com/news/1046f613-8e0d-4326-bd38-2d90a094e2cb

claims.quote: could that happen in the US? Yes
claims.claim: [An interview subject, asked whether Korea's crash could happen in the US,] said yes.
claims.basis: Opinion/prediction expressed by an interview subject, not an independently checkable factual claim.

claims.quote: the president of South Korea held an emergency intervention for their stock market
claims.claim: The president of South Korea held an emergency intervention meeting for the stock market during the crash.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: President Lee Jae-myung chaired emergency market-stabilization meetings on consecutive days in mid-July 2026. https://finance.biggo.com/news/7ad8eab6-912f-404e-8a02-ad02ad389774

claims.quote: there's about 51 million people
claims.claim: South Korea has a population of about 51 million people.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Approximately 51.7 million per current population estimates. https://www.worldometers.info/world-population/south-korea-population/

claims.quote: 14 million of them, or one in four, are what's called retail investors
claims.claim: 14 million South Koreans, or one in four people, are retail investors.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: 14M / ~51.7M ≈ 27%, consistent with 'one in four' (25%). Internal arithmetic on the video's own population and investor-count figures.

claims.quote: housing in South Korea has become so expensive that for a lot of young people, owning a home stopped being a realistic goal
claims.claim: Housing in South Korea has become so expensive that owning a home stopped being a realistic goal for many young people.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Youth (under-39) homeownership fell to a record-low 27.7%; Seoul price-to-income ratio ~13.9 years vs 6.3 nationwide. https://en.sedaily.com/finance/2026/07/26/youth-home-ownership-falls-to-record-low-of-277-percent

claims.quote: one of their biggest finance influencers actually said that their last chance to build wealth is the stock market
claims.claim: An unnamed major South Korean finance influencer said the stock market is people's last chance to build wealth, or they'll get left behind.
claims.label: unverifiable
claims.basis: The influencer is never named in the video, so there is no specific person or quote to check against a source. Unverifiable by construction.

claims.quote: Her portfolio was worth over $650,000, and she was up 150%
claims.claim: An anonymous investor featured in an unnamed documentary had a portfolio worth over $650,000, up 150%, mostly in leveraged ETFs, and hid the extent of her leverage from her family.
claims.label: unverifiable
claims.basis: Anonymous subject in an unnamed documentary, holding private brokerage information; no independent record located to verify or refute. Unverifiable by construction.

claims.quote: Koreans invested about 10 trillion won into leveraged funds betting on just one company
claims.claim: At its peak, South Korean investors had put about 10 trillion won into leveraged funds betting on a single company.
claims.label: plausible
claims.basis: Samsung + SK Hynix single-stock leveraged ETFs held about 14tn won AUM by mid-June 2026 and drew about 23tn won of cumulative inflows; a single-company breakdown near 10tn won is the right order of magnitude but is not pinned to an exact published per-company figure. https://finance.biggo.com/news/fcf12162-d59e-41d9-8384-a5a0bdfa6b23

claims.quote: the two companies that dominate that market are Samsung and SK Hynix
claims.claim: Samsung and SK Hynix dominate the global memory-chip market that supplies AI data centers.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Q1 2026: Samsung 38% + SK Hynix 29% ≈ 67% of global DRAM; SK Hynix 58% + Samsung 21% ≈ 79% of HBM. https://counterpointresearch.com/en/insights/global-dram-and-hbm-market-share

claims.quote: they have spent $376 billion on AI infrastructure in 2025
claims.claim: [Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Meta] spent $376 billion on AI infrastructure in 2025.
claims.label: plausible
claims.basis: Combined Big Four 2025 capex figures cluster around $378-410bn depending on whether a narrower 'AI infrastructure' or broader total-capex definition is used; $376B sits just below the commonly cited ~$378bn figure. https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/big-tech/big-techs-ai-spending-plans-reach-725-billion

claims.quote: they're on track to spend 725 billion
claims.claim: In 2026, [Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Meta] are on track to spend $725 billion on AI infrastructure.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: $725bn planned 2026 capex across the Big Four is consistently reported: Amazon ~$200bn, Microsoft ~$190bn, Alphabet $175-185bn, Meta $115-135bn. https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/big-tech/big-techs-ai-spending-plans-reach-725-billion

claims.quote: They were just named the number one data removal service by Wirecutter
claims.claim: DeleteMe was named the number one data removal service by Wirecutter.
claims.label: unverifiable
claims.basis: Searches for a Wirecutter data-removal-service ranking did not locate one; Wirecutter/NYT content is also known to be difficult for automated web search to reach directly, so this is better described as unreached than as absent. Third-party 2026 roundups more often rank a different service first.

claims.quote: removed over 68 instances of someone selling my info
claims.claim: DeleteMe scanned thousands of listings and removed over 68 instances of the narrator's personal information being sold, saving him an estimated 14.5 hours.
claims.label: unverifiable
claims.basis: A private account dashboard belonging to the presenter, who is paid to promote the product; not independently checkable.

claims.quote: That is America's biggest chip maker
claims.claim: [Referring to Micron] Micron is America's biggest chip maker.
claims.label: false
claims.basis: Nvidia is the largest US semiconductor company by both market cap (~$4.85-5.3T in mid-2026) and revenue, roughly 5x Micron's market cap (~$983B-$1T); Micron ranks around 6th among US chip firms overall. Micron IS America's biggest memory-chip maker specifically, which is the qualified claim the argument actually needed. https://www.statista.com/statistics/283359/top-20-semiconductor-companies/

claims.quote: the US has sort of popped the bubble in Korea
claims.claim: The United States caused ('popped') South Korea's stock market crash: US chip stocks sold off first in late June 2026, nervous ahead of Micron's earnings, and that decline then triggered Korea's crash, 'except way harder'.
claims.label: misleading
claims.basis: Micron fell 13% on June 23, 2026 — the same day as Korea's own 'Black Tuesday' — and Forbes attributes that US chip selloff to South Korea's own Financial Supervisory Service warning about risky leveraged ETFs tracking Samsung/SK Hynix (and Micron), not the reverse. Micron's own earnings the next day beat and the stock rose. The two markets moved together on the same day, originating from a Korean regulatory warning; the video's one-directional 'the US popped it' framing reverses the more-supported direction of causation. https://www.forbes.com/sites/antoniopequenoiv/2026/06/23/micron-tumbles-13-as-south-korean-etf-warning-fuels-chip-sell-off/

claims.quote: in one session, the KOSPI dropped something like 4.6%
claims.claim: In one trading session [in late June/July 2026], the KOSPI dropped something like 4.6%.
claims.label: plausible
claims.basis: No session in the crash window closed at exactly -4.6%; nearest matches are -4.91% (7 Jul), -4.52% (10 Jun), -4.46% (20 Jul) — the hedged 'something like 4.6%' is in the right range without an exact match. Yahoo Finance ^KS11 daily closes.

claims.quote: Samsung and SK Hynix both went down more than 9% in just one day
claims.claim: A week after the initial late-June selloff, Samsung and SK Hynix both fell more than 9% in a single day.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Confirmed with a wide margin on multiple days in the crash window: June 23, Samsung -12.31%, SK Hynix -12.47%; July 13, Samsung -10.70%, SK Hynix -15.37%. Exchange price data (^KS11 constituents).

claims.quote: the KOSPI went down more than 10% in just a day
claims.claim: On the day Koreans are calling 'Black Tuesday' [June 23, 2026], the KOSPI went down more than 10% in a single day.
claims.label: misleading
claims.basis: The pre-publication 'Black Tuesday' (June 23, 2026) closed at -9.99%, and the close was also the day's intraday low, so it never crossed -10% at any point in the session. A KOSPI day worse than -10% (-10.84%) did occur on July 28, 2026, but that was 8 days after this video published, so it is not the day being described. https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/more/261984032-stock-kospi-nekki-kioxia-samsung-skhynix-tradingkey

claims.quote: one of the worst drops in the whole history of the Korean stock market
claims.claim: The Black Tuesday KOSPI drop was one of the worst drops in the whole history of the Korean stock market.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: The -9.99% session triggered a circuit breaker, the first since March 2020, and ranks among the KOSPI's handful of worst sessions on record.

claims.quote: a 10% one-day drop in the US stock market, that would be the third worst day in American history, only behind 1987 and the Great Depression
claims.claim: A 10% one-day drop in the US stock market would be the third-worst day in American history, behind only 1987 (Black Monday) and the Great Depression.
claims.label: false
claims.basis: The ranking omits March 16, 2020 (COVID crash), when the S&P 500 fell -12.0% (Dow -12.9%) — worse than a 10% drop, and neither 1987 nor the Depression. A -10% day lands around 4th-6th on the all-time list, not 3rd. https://landmarkwealthmgmt.com/articles/10-worst-sp-500-one-day-declines-1981-2025-what-the-data-reveals-about-market-crashes-and-recoveries/

claims.quote: about 2% of Korean margin accounts get force liquidated. But during this crash, that number went higher than 10%, which is about five times the normal rate
claims.claim: Under normal conditions, about 2% of Korean margin accounts get force-liquidated; during the KOSPI crash, that rate exceeded 10%, about five times the normal rate.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Forced-liquidation rate averaged about 2.1% over the six months before the crisis, surged above 10% the week of July 10, 2026. 10/2.1 ≈ 4.8x, consistent with 'about five times'. https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/south-korean-stock-market-faces-margin-call-crisis-july-forced-liquidation-reaches-3-442-trillion-krw

claims.quote: they have to rebalance every day, which means at the end of a big down day, the fund has to sell into a falling market to maintain its leverage ratio
claims.claim: [Leveraged ETFs] have to rebalance every day, meaning at the end of a big down day, the fund must sell into a falling market to maintain its leverage ratio.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Leveraged ETFs reset exposure daily via swaps/futures: if the underlying index falls, the fund must sell additional exposure at the close to maintain its target leverage ratio — a well-documented structural feature of these products. https://www.fundssociety.com/en/news/markets/equities-leveraged-etfs-and-the-mechanics-of-market-declines/

claims.quote: more than 600 billion dollars got erased from Asian markets
claims.claim: Over the two days following Korea's crash, more than $600 billion was erased from Asian stock markets.
claims.label: plausible
claims.basis: No single published figure was found for this exact two-day Asian total; a back-of-envelope check (a -9.99% KOSPI day on a ~$2.1T market ≈ $210B, plus Nikkei/Taiwan/Hong Kong losses) puts $600B in a plausible range but does not pin the number to a cited total.

claims.quote: Japan went down more than 4%
claims.claim: In the two days following Korea's crash, Japan's stock market went down more than 4%.
claims.label: misleading
claims.basis: The Nikkei fell -3.55% on June 23 (the day of Korea's Black Tuesday), then -0.88% and +4.61% over the following two sessions — it did not clear -4% on the days this passage describes. A >4% Nikkei day did occur later in the episode (-4.15% Jun 26, -4.03% Jul 17), so the figure exists but is attached to the wrong days. https://www.asiafinancial.com/kospi-nikkei-hang-seng-sink-as-tech-doubts-rock-asia-again

claims.quote: the market was literally closed for a national holiday
claims.claim: At one point, the only thing that stopped the KOSPI from falling further was that the market was closed for a national holiday.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: The Korea Exchange closed Friday, July 17, 2026 for Constitution Day, immediately after a -6.37% session on July 16. https://www.ibtimes.com.au/korea-exchange-closure-constitution-day-impact-1872448

claims.quote: who by the way was the same person who spent a year encouraging people to get into the stock market
claims.claim: South Korea's president, who called the emergency market intervention, is the same person who spent the preceding year encouraging citizens to invest in the stock market.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: President Lee Jae-myung campaigned on a 'KOSPI 5,000' pledge and described himself as a retail investor; the index rose sharply during his push for retail participation before the crash. https://fortune.com/2026/08/02/kospi-rout-korea-stock-market-volatility-sk-hynix-samsung-leveraged-etf/

claims.quote: every time US margin debt went to an extreme, a crash happened almost right after, every single time
claims.claim: US margin debt has spiked to an extreme before nearly every major US stock market crash (cited: 1968, 1972, 1987, 2000, 2007, 2018, 2021), a pattern the video says has held every single time.
claims.label: misleading
claims.basis: The named peaks are real for the periods independently checkable — margin debt did top out near the 2000 (~2.6-2.8% GDP), 2007 (~2.5-3.0%), and 2021 (~3.8-4.0%) cyclical highs, each followed by a correction; the 1968/1972/2018 data points were not independently verified here or in either prior reading. But margin debt is widely characterized as a coincident indicator of risk appetite rather than a leading/timing signal — it rises with the market and can stay elevated for extended periods without a crash following, so a chart that only marks extremes actually followed by crashes overstates the reliability of the pattern as a predictor. https://realinvestmentadvice.com/resources/blog/margin-debt-risk-the-ratios-that-mislead-investors/

claims.quote: US margin debt just hit roughly 4 and 1/2% of GDP. That is the highest level ever recorded in American history
claims.claim: As of June 2026, US margin debt hit roughly 4½% of GDP, the highest level ever recorded in American history.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: FINRA margin debt / GDP was 4.71% in June 2026, a record high; 'roughly 4½%' rounds down slightly but is directionally accurate. https://www.gurufocus.com/economic_indicators/4266/finra-investor-margin-debt-relative-to-gdp

claims.quote: higher than the dot-com bubble, higher than 2007, higher than even the 2021 meme stock everything bubble, and it's higher by a lot
claims.claim: US margin debt in June 2026 (4.71% of GDP) is higher than the dot-com bubble peak, the 2007 peak, and the 2021 meme-stock peak, by a significant margin.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Prior cyclical peaks: ~2.6-2.8% (2000), ~2.5-3.0% (2007), ~3.8-4.0% (2021), vs. 4.71% now — roughly 20-25% above the 2021 peak and 65-80% above 2000. https://www.gurufocus.com/economic_indicators/4266/finra-investor-margin-debt-relative-to-gdp

claims.quote: the official margin data only tracks one kind of borrowing, which is traditional margin loans at brokerage accounts
claims.claim: Official US margin-debt statistics only track traditional brokerage margin loans, missing leveraged ETFs, options, portfolio margin, and private credit as sources of market leverage.
claims.label: misleading
claims.basis: Right in substance for leveraged-ETF embedded leverage, options notional, and non-broker private credit — none of those appear in the standard FINRA margin-debt series. But portfolio-margin debit balances ARE reported to FINRA under Rule 4210(g)/4521, so including 'portfolio margin' among the blind spots is inaccurate. https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/key-topics/margin-accounts

claims.quote: We have zero-day options where people gamble on what the stock market does in the next 6 hours. They're all trading at record volumes
claims.claim: Zero-day options (0DTE), where people gamble on stock-market moves within hours, are trading at record volumes.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: 0DTE options hit record monthly-average volumes in 2026 (e.g., SPX 0DTE ~3.0M contracts/day, 63% of SPX options volume, up from ~5% in 2016). https://www.ifre.com/topic-codes/2321645/zero-day-contracts-become-dominant-force-in-sp-500-options-market

claims.quote: Every time their CapEx spending goes up, their stock goes up as well
claims.claim: Every time a hyperscaler's AI capex spending guidance goes up, its stock goes up as well.
claims.label: plausible
claims.basis: Broadly consistent with 2024-2026 hyperscaler earnings-reaction patterns, where raised capex guidance has generally been rewarded by markets, but 'every time' is a strong absolute claim not checked here against a complete price-reaction dataset across all relevant earnings calls.

claims.quote: it's gone from as a group 40% a year and a half ago to about 20% today
claims.claim: Jim Chanos said hyperscaler returns on incremental AI investment have gone from about 40% as a group a year and a half ago to about 20% today, heading toward 10%.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Chanos is widely and consistently quoted making this exact claim about hyperscaler incremental ROIC declining from 40% to 20% and sliding toward 10%. https://www.benzinga.com/markets/prediction-markets/26/07/60841557/enron-short-seller-jim-chanos-sees-a-1999-type-moment-in-ai-boom-includes-spcx-tsla-in-his-shorts

claims.quote: they still lose tens of billions of
claims.claim: [OpenAI and Anthropic] still lose tens of billions of dollars a year.
claims.label: misleading
claims.basis: True for OpenAI (~$14B projected loss in 2026 on ~$34B+ spend). Not true for Anthropic in the relevant window: Anthropic was on track for its first-ever quarterly operating profit (~$559M on $10.9B projected revenue) in Q2 2026, the same period this video covers — a sharp reversal from earlier guidance that did not expect full-year profitability until 2028. Lumping both companies together as 'still losing tens of billions' overstates Anthropic's financial position at the time. https://www.pymnts.com/artificial-intelligence-2/2026/anthropic-on-track-for-first-operating-profit-as-revenue-surges/

claims.quote: they make up 70 to 80% of all the AI compute demand
claims.claim: [OpenAI and Anthropic] together make up 70 to 80% of all AI compute demand.
claims.label: false
claims.basis: Epoch AI (the leading independent tracker of AI compute allocation): OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI COMBINED used only about 20-30% (best estimate ~21%) of global AI compute capacity by the end of 2025; OpenAI alone was ~10-15%. The video's 70-80% figure overstates this by roughly 3-3.5x, and this is the number the 'unprofitable AI labs hold up the whole pyramid' argument depends on. https://epoch.ai/gradient-updates/frontier-labs-dont-use-most-ai-compute

claims.quote: which happens to be the revenue of Nvidia, of Micron, and of the whole AI
claims.claim: The ~$725B/year hyperscalers are spending on AI happens to roughly equal the revenue of Nvidia, of Micron, and of the whole AI trade.
claims.basis: Genuinely ambiguous as stated: it isn't clear whether 'the revenue of Nvidia, of Micron, and of the whole AI trade' means each entity's revenue separately equals ~$725B, that their sum equals it, or that 'the whole AI trade' is a notional sector aggregate subsuming the other two. These readings settle very differently — Nvidia's FY2026 revenue alone was ~$216B, nowhere near $725B on its own — and the sentence does not disambiguate which reading is intended, so no single ground truth can be checked against it.

claims.quote: IPOs have come to market at over 12% of GDP in post-IPO market cap
claims.claim: In 2026, IPOs have come to market at over 12% of GDP in post-IPO market cap, more than double the previous record of 5% set at the dot-com bubble peak.
claims.label: unverifiable
claims.basis: Multiple search angles (the specific metric, Goldman Sachs's dot-com-comparison research, 2026 mega-IPO coverage) did not locate this 'post-IPO market cap as % of GDP' series or confirm the 5%/12% figures. Circumstantial support exists (e.g., SpaceX alone listed around $1.7-2.4T, several percent of US GDP by itself), and Goldman's own 2026 IPO-market read said issuance 'still falls short of bubble territory', which is in tension with the video's framing. Ground truth for the precise stat could not be established.

claims.quote: the first hyperscaler to cut back on AI spending will be rewarded by the market
claims.claim: [Unnamed] analysts/investors are saying the first hyperscaler to cut back on AI spending will be rewarded by the market rather than punished.
claims.label: unverifiable
claims.basis: The subject ('they') is never identified — no named analyst, firm, or report — so there is no specific claim to verify against a source. Unverifiable by construction.

claims.quote: In the year 2000, Coca-Cola needed 10,000 routers from Cisco. By 2001, they needed only 2,000
claims.claim: In 2000, Coca-Cola ordered 10,000 routers from Cisco; by 2001, its order had dropped to only 2,000, contributing to Cisco's earnings collapse.
claims.label: unverifiable
claims.basis: Independent web searches (both for the claim as stated and for Cisco's real 2001 customer-cancellation history) found extensive real coverage of Cisco's dot-com-era inventory collapse and demand cancellations, but zero mention of Coca-Cola, 10,000 routers, or 2,000 routers anywhere. The absence of any public footprint for a specific, named, checkable business anecdote is a fabrication-tell pattern, but is not proof of invention — no record was found either way.

claims.quote: the NASDAQ went down 78%
claims.claim: The NASDAQ fell 78% in the dot-com bust that followed.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASDAQ Composite fell approximately 78% from its March 10, 2000 peak (5,048.62) to its October 2002 trough (~1,114-1,140). https://internationalbanker.com/history-of-financial-crises/the-dotcom-bubble-burst-2000/

claims.quote: Shrek 5 scheduled to be released June 2027
claims.claim: Shrek 5 is scheduled to be released in June 2027.
